comment: Values approximate; verify against NASA sources.
notes: Code generated with AI assistance (Claude). Reviewed by team. The delta-v map from the old Sim Spec section 2, as data. All values in m/s. A mission profile lists the legs flown outbound and, if the mission needs a return, the return legs. Required delta-v = outbound legs - Earth rotation bonus (if the profile allows it) + orbit raise (Hohmann from the parking orbit) + return legs, all times (1 + margin).

earth_rotation.source: Old Sim Spec section 2 (launch site bonus). Earth's equatorial rotation speed is about 465 m/s.

margins.source: safe_range_ratio is from Sim Spec v2 section 2.3. default_margin_fraction (3%) is MADE UP: the spec says 'plus a margin' without a number.

loss_model.formula: required = v_insert(target perigee, vis-viva) - spin bonus + g0 * (k_first * first-stage burn time + k_upper * upper-stage burn times) + k_drag * first-stage drag loss (vertical-ascent estimate), x (1 + margin)
loss_model.source: Calibrated against Juno I / Explorer 1; launch sim will replace this estimate. gravity_loss_coeff_first_stage is CALIBRATED: the realistic Juno-class (reference_rockets.json) flying the lofted profile reaches Explorer 1's ~358 x 2,550 km orbit with a 2% margin (range ratio 1.02 including the 3% game margin). It also absorbs everything the estimate leaves out (the real pitched, lofted trajectory and the real Juno's hydyne uprate), so it is a fitted number, not a measured one. drag_loss_coeff 1.0 uses the vertical-ascent drag estimate (Cd x area / mass, integrated) as is: MADE UP. gravity_loss_coeff_upper 0.2 (upper stages of a normal ascent still climb a little) is MADE UP. Lofted profile: liftoff <= 50 t and every upper stage a kick stage (vacuum TWR >= 5) is a MADE UP rule for small rockets like Juno; its kick stages fire horizontally at the top of the lofted coast, so their gravity loss is 0.
